title: Total existence from a lower first-degree bound and nonnegative second degree
statement: Let C be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], K a Z×Z bicomplex [def-sp-double-complex-total], and a an integer. Assume K^{p,q} is a zero object whenever p<a or q<0. Then the diagonal coproducts required for K.HasTotal(up Z) exist.

source.place: Section Double complexes and associated total complexes, definition-associated-simple-complex; finite-diagonal clause, also Definition 015H(1)-(2)

proof.text: For fixed n take the subtype of diagonal indices p+q=n with a≤p and 0≤q. Projection to p injects it into the finite interval [a,n]. Form the finite coproduct of these terms. Its cofan on the full diagonal has the canonical inclusion on this subtype and zero maps elsewhere. Every omitted term is zero by one of the two bounds. Any cofan descends uniquely by the finite coproduct universal property, and the omitted terms satisfy its equations by their zero-object property. Thus the full diagonal coproduct exists, for every n, which is HasTotal. This includes n<a, where the subtype is empty.

proof_origin.place: Section Double complexes and associated total complexes, definition-associated-simple-complex; finite-diagonal clause, also Definition 015H(1)-(2)
